title: Part 1.II — Antinomies of Definition
ocr_notes: Chapter has italic-tl ABBYY-cluster issues. Normalized for this analysis: 'std' → 'stā' (Sanskrit/Indo-Germanic root, book p.21); 'explicidy' → 'explicitly'; 'sufficiendy' → 'sufficiently'; 'elementaiism' → 'elementarism' (book p.57, in the Korzybski note); 'Cariolanus' → 'Coriolanus' (Index, out of scope). Italic technical terms (kath' auto, sub specie aeternitatis, omnis determinatio est negatio, hypostasis, hypokeimenon, hypotithēmi, ratio seminales, ta pathēmata mathēmata, intelligere est pati, esse est percipi, causa sui, L'état c'est moi) verified against context.

outline.summary: The Indo-Germanic root *sthā- (Sanskrit sthā) underlies a Stance-family vocabulary — consist, constancy, constitution, contrast, destiny, ecstasy, existence, hypostatize, obstacle, stage, state, status, statute, stead, subsist, substance, system; in German stellen, surfacing in Vorstellung. Etymologically, sub-stance designates what stands beneath or supports a thing — therefore something extrinsic, contextual, outside the thing — although it is conventionally used to designate what a thing intrinsically is. This is the chapter's foundational paradox: the word for the intrinsic etymologically refers to the extrinsic.

outline.section: Locke and the Impairment of Substance
outline.summary: Locke (Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Bk II, Ch XXIII, 'Of Our Complex Ideas of Substances') impaired the term's prestige by exposing its incoherence: pressed for the support of qualities, the user can only answer 'something — he knows not what,' like the Indian's elephant supported by a tortoise supported by what-he-knows-not. But banishing the term, Burke argues, merely conceals its functions; dramatism re-examines its embarrassments and potentialities for transformation. The Greek hypostasis (literally 'standing under') and Latin substantia carry the same paradox; hypostasis also has medical senses ('sediment, lees, dregs, grounds') that Freud's 'cloacal' motives illuminate when probing for fundamentals.

To define (de-finire, to mark boundaries) is to place a thing in terms of something else — its context. Strategic 'alchemy': here intrinsic and extrinsic can change places. Spinoza is the paradigm — for Spinoza, only the total scene (nature = God) can be 'in itself' (kath' auto, id quod per se concipitur); single objects are 'defined' by the totality surrounding them, so 'omnis determinatio est negatio' (all determination is negation). Examples: Southern Agrarians 'taking their stand in Dixie' (a stand in Dixie versus a stand for Dixie reveals the act-agent / scene-purpose ambiguity); the historicist who 'dissolves man into nature' versus the formalist who treats works 'in themselves.'

A second strategy: defining substance by ancestral cause — biological descent, tribal, genetic. Natura (from nasci, 'to be born'), physis ('to grow'), Aristotle's genus, the Christian derivation of mankind from God, Nazi blood-philosophy, and Plato's theory of forms (each thing imitating its eponym in heaven) are familial-substance strategies. The mediaeval universalia question (ante rem / in re / post rem) gets a Burkean dramatist gloss: realist, Aristotelian (entelechy as potentiality-for-being-fully-of-the-class), nominalist. The cluster of 'general, generic, genetic, genitive' marks the gradation from biological-familial to logical-classificatory; 'generic' fades the tribal connotation, 'general' nearly extinguishes it.

Burke surveys characteristic forms the grammar of substance may embody as particular calculi. The major species enumerated: geometric, familial, directional, dialectic; with subspecies / cross-cuts including nutritive (transubstantiation), class-substance, divisive substance, and the directional cluster (motion / movement / cause / emotion / moment) inside motivation. The taxonomy is non-exclusive: each calculus is a 'way of placement' that can be combined with the others.

The over-all category. Treats human motives in terms of verbal/symbolic action; derives its character from the systematic contemplation of antinomies — i.e. the recognition that we necessarily define a thing in terms of something else. Agon (protagonist defined by antagonist) is its sharpest instance; rivales as opposite banks of the same stream (Coleridge); 'we become the image of the thing we hate' (G. Russell). The most thoroughgoing dialectical pair is Being / Not-Being — Plotinus's negative theology derives the divine substance only by negation of all material attributes, an abstract Oneness reached by transcending the familial and the geometric.

When a term is purified by abstraction, it tends to its negation: God as 'pure' or 'absolute' Person is impersonal — Pure Personality = No Personality. Pure Being = Not-Being (Hegel); Aristotle's God as Pure Act or as eternal, unchangeable repose; Leibniz's 'virtual innateness'; Hegelian 'pure direction' (Parker Tyler glossing Julien Gracq's Château d'Argol); the 'witheriness of withinness' or 'atop the atop' (Marvell, Melville). Pure escape = perpetual imprisonment in escape. Class-, national-, or collective motives technically become 'pure' when set against an individual locus — yielding 'split substance' (the patriot-soldier killing 'national' rather than 'personal' enemies).

Galileo's experimental 'ordeal' is dialectical-agonistic: knowledge through the act of assertion that 'suffers' a counter-assertion called forth from the act's context. This is the tragic pattern: action → corresponding passion → understanding (mathēma) transcending the act. Burke glosses the Greek proverb ta pathēmata mathēmata ('the suffered is the learned') and reconstructs it as a triad — poiēma (act/deed/poem), pathēma (suffering, passive state, condition), mathēma (the learned, knowledge, the mathematical). Hegelian dialectic: a series of dyings as progress toward greater self-realization. Scholastic intelligere est pati ('to understand is to be affected by'), contrasted with Berkeley's esse est percipi (which reverses the direction by treating actuality in terms of knowledge).

Reducing the poiēma/pathēma/mathēma triad to a dyad yields the actus/status pair: act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith (pistis, fides) as act and knowledge (gnōsis, intellectus) as the state derived from the act. Philological case-study: aretē/virtus from Ares (war-god) — originally 'prowess,' active; gradually becoming potentialities-for-action, then states of mind, then sheer negations ('not killing, not stealing'). 'Hero' undergoes the same drift: first one who does heroic things; then one with potentialities for heroic action; then one in the state-of-being-a-hero by reputation/inheritance. Class-substance: occupational acts develop properties → properties harden into status. Kingship begins as an act (heroic deed) and becomes inherited state ('L'état c'est moi' = the king's substance and the State's substance merged). Actus/status also maps onto potentiality/actuality.

All gods are 'substances' — names for motives or combinations of motives. Polytheism distributes scenic motives across local gods (river-motive vs. mountain-motive); universal religions consolidate them, enabling commerce by giving believers an overall substance carried across scenes (hypostasis preserves personal identity across local motivational textures). The monotheistic motive shades into its secular analogue — the monetary motive ('the One God or the Gold Standard'). Marxist calculus: industrial workers share the 'factory situation' as universal scene, defining their substance as 'wage slavery,' splitting the universal motive into the two classes (possessors / dispossessed). Sheer work is 'motion'; it becomes actus only when understood through socialist organization. The Marxian state will not 'wither away' because actus and status are grammatically inseparable.

Material properties as 'state' brings actus/status in line with intrinsic/extrinsic. Hegel's Philosophy of History equates Matter with the extrinsic (gravity, externally referred), Spirit with the intrinsic (Bei-sich-selbst-sein, self-contained existence). But the distinction subtly inverts when Hegel makes the State 'the materialization of Spirit' — an antithesis-merger; whichever pole one stresses governs the reading (whence the Marxist reversal of Hegel). Korzybski's 'inside the skin / outside the skin' distinction repeats this paradox. The gerontologist's 'intrinsic resistance to disease,' once made manipulable by external chemicals, dissolves into the extrinsic — body is chemistry, all outside the body is chemistry, the intrinsic dissolves into chemical scene. Spinoza's causa sui (substance as cause of itself) marks the limit: humanist strategy treats man as causa sui with intrinsic dignity, supernaturalist strategy derives that dignity from God as ancestor. The intrinsic must not be confused with the unique — a poet's intrinsic value resides also in attributes shared with many other poets ('the differentiated also has significant attributes as members of its class').

The ambiguity of substance affords a major resource of rhetoric. 'It is substantially true' is regularly deployable when 'it is not true' is more accurate; a slave is 'substantially free' by inherited qualities; a proposal can be accepted 'in principle' (where 'principle' is etymologically a 'first,' an origin) to skirt embarrassing endorsement. Positivists who outlaw substance smuggle it back in via 'in principle' (only-possible-in-principle scientific proof) and 'universally valid.' A judge ruled a petition 'substantially fraudulent' because mixed; reversed because the genuine signatures considered in themselves sufficed. Substantive rhetoric also operates without telltale markers — wherever one defines someone or some position by ancestral, contextual, or familial means without flagging the act.

Because the five pentad terms can be considered as 'principles' with margins of overlap, a thinker can use one term as the point of departure in two opposite directions: (i) consistent — derive consequences from the term's nature (e.g., naturalism originally derived from man-in-nature); (ii) compensatory — depart from the term toward its near-antithesis (e.g., 'naturalism' became the name for a technology-and-money philosophy nearly antithetical to nature; 'personalism' affirms the person where the person is not in fact paramount). The first 'reasons by a therefore,' the second 'reasons by a however.' This grammar lets thinkers retain the prestige of a god-term while building structures that depart from it; by the time the departure is obvious, the new order can stand without the old anchor.

Modern science's abandonment of substance and causality is itself a 'dialectical enterprise designed to transcend terminologies of action and substance.' But action is what we live; treating action only as motion is 'gross misrepresentation.' Concession: the pentad need not be the philosopher's stone, but it is 'a philosopher's stone for the synopsis of writings that have sought the philosopher's stone.' Closing thesis: substantiation is not an illusion but a citable reality — tactics of injury and gratification employ it constantly (calling a man 'friend' proclaims consubstantiality, calling him 'bastard' attacks his familial authorship). An epithet assigns substance doubly: it characterizes the object and implies an action toward it, thus serving as motive.

substance_types.label: Paradox of substance (general)
substance_types.gloss: The structural irony at the root of all substance-talk: the word designates what a thing intrinsically is, but etymologically refers to something outside the thing that stands beneath or supports it. Every substance-claim therefore covertly imports a contextual reference into an intrinsic claim.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Locke's 'something I know not what'; the tortoise-supporting-the-elephant regress (book p. 22).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Names the master-irony from which the chapter's whole taxonomy is derived: every substance-claim oscillates between intrinsic and extrinsic poles.
substance_types.related_pentad_term: all five (the substance grammar cross-cuts the pentad)

substance_types.label: Contextual (positional, geometric, definitional) substance
substance_types.gloss: Definition by placement of a thing within its context, location, or surroundings. To define is to mark boundaries (de-finire), and to mark boundaries requires reference to what is outside the thing. Maximalist version: Spinoza's universal substance, where each object is determined by the totality (omnis determinatio est negatio).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Spinoza on substance and nature/God; Southern Agrarians 'I'll Take My Stand' as a stand 'in Dixie' (book pp. 24-25).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Treats the thing as 'in terms of' its scene; intrinsic / extrinsic swap places at the boundary; pairs like heredity/environment, mind/matter, mechanism/teleology each take one term as the other's 'context.'

substance_types.label: Geometric substance
substance_types.gloss: A subspecies of contextual substance: an object placed in its setting via logical-spatial relations from which everything else is 'necessarily' derivable; Euclidean-Spinozistic implicit-relation calculus. Plastic enough to slide into materialist determinism (Dreiser's 'chemism').
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Spinoza's geometric method; Dreiser's view of motives as 'chemism' (book p. 29).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Reduces motive to inevitable derivations within a closed scenic totality; the dialectical antinomy is that 'necessity' here is purchased by erasing the agent.

substance_types.label: Familial (tribal, ancestral) substance
substance_types.gloss: Defining a substance by ancestral cause — biological descent or any 'spiritualized' analogue (covenant, founder, eponym, creation). Includes Plato's archetypal forms (each thing imitating its eponym in heaven) and Aristotle's entelechy (the individual as actualization of its class).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Christian derivation of humanity from God; Plato's theory of forms; Nazi blood-philosophy; the cluster 'general / generic / genetic / genitive' (book pp. 26-28).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Stresses derivation rather than placement; mediaeval universalia debate (ante rem / in re / post rem) is its dialectical-realist / Aristotelian / nominalist refraction.

substance_types.label: Directional substance
substance_types.gloss: Substance characterized by motion toward, by 'the way,' by direction-from-within. Strongly futuristic and purposive ('Where are you going?' rather than 'Where are you from?'). Includes the cluster motion / movement / cause / emotion / moment as variant glosses on motivation.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Tendencies, trends; immigrants as part of a 'westward movement'; I.A. Richards's pun on emotion as motion (book pp. 31-32).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Converts 'free' motion into determined motion via statistical regularity; reveals the substantial paradox in 'tendency' (a tendency to do X is by the same token a tendency not to do X).

substance_types.label: Nutritive (transubstantial) substance
substance_types.gloss: A merger of contextual and familial substance grounded in the consumption of external elements that become internal — eating as transubstantiation. The organism's environment becomes its consubstantiality.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Eucharist; totemic rites; Coates's 'Eater of Darkness'; manganese as 'mother love chemical' (book pp. 30-31).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Dissolves the morphological boundary between organism and environment (Angyal's biosphere; Bernard's 'internal environment').

substance_types.label: Dialectic substance
substance_types.gloss: The over-all category: substance arising from the systematic contemplation of the antinomies — the recognition that we necessarily define a thing in terms of something else, where the something else is not merely an other but the other (the antagonist, the agon). It is the dramatistic super-category that covers the rest.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Agon in tragedy and politics; Coleridge's 'rivales as opposite banks of the same stream'; 'we become the image of the thing we hate' (book pp. 33-34).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Treats motive in terms of verbal/symbolic action; the cultural accretions of language become a 'second nature' intrinsic to agents as agents.

substance_types.label: Substance under the paradox of purity (pure substance)
substance_types.gloss: When a substance is purified by abstraction to its absolute, it tends toward its negation: God as 'pure person' is impersonal; pure being is not-being; pure escape is perpetual imprisonment in escape; class-motive becomes pure when set against the individual.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Plotinus's negative theology (One reached by negating the material); Hegel's pure being / not-being; Aristotle's Pure Act = eternal repose (book pp. 35-37).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Identifies an asymptote where any term, intensified to absolute purity, flips into its dialectical antithesis — the formal engine of negative theology and 'witheriness of withinness.'

substance_types.label: Divisive (split) substance
substance_types.gloss: A subspecies of the paradox of purity: the agent is divided into 'two substances' by competing motivational scenes — typically a collective/universal scene against an individual scene. The same person acts under one substance qua patriot and another qua individual.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Soldier killing nationally but not individually; the man with one substance at work and another at home as 'split personality' (book p. 37).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Names the formal mechanism by which an agent is multiply substantial, anchoring later analyses of identification and ideology.

substance_types.label: Tragic-dialectic substance (poiēma / pathēma / mathēma)
substance_types.gloss: Substance constituted through the tragic triad: the act (poiēma) calls forth a counter-assertion from its context which the agent suffers (pathēma); from the suffered comes knowledge (mathēma) that transcends the original act. Substance here is what is left when act, suffering, and learning fuse into character.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Greek proverb ta pathēmata mathēmata; Galileo's experimental 'ordeal'; Hegelian succession of self-realizing dyings; scholastic intelligere est pati (book pp. 38-41).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Merges intrinsic and extrinsic motivations at the moment of tragic vision — the fatal accident becomes representative of the agent's character.

substance_types.label: Actus / status substance (act and state)
substance_types.gloss: The dyadic reduction of the tragic triad: act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith-as-act vs. knowledge-as-state. The pair maps onto potentiality / actuality and tracks the philological transformation by which active terms (aretē, virtus, hero) drift into states of being or sheer negations.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Aretē/virtus from Ares — 'prowess' to potentiality to state of mind to not-killing; hero from doer-of-deeds to inherited reputation; kingship from heroic act to inheritable state — 'L'état c'est moi' (book pp. 41-43).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Maps directly onto the Act-Agent ratio: where the chapter's substance vocabulary articulates with the pentad most tightly. Class-substance follows by the same logic (occupational acts harden into class status).

substance_types.label: Class (occupational) substance
substance_types.gloss: A sociological refraction of actus/status: occupational acts develop characteristic properties, and over time these properties harden into class-defining states. Ruling classes pass from a regime in which act and status are co-balanced into one where inherited position eclipses any continuing act.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Nobility derived from horsemanship-in-war turning to pageantry and sport; kingship becoming sheer inheritable state (book p. 42).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Anchors the actus/status pair sociologically; provides the formal grammar for diagnosing the petrification of action into property.

substance_types.label: Universal motive as substance (the One God / Gold Standard)
substance_types.gloss: When a substance becomes a universal motive, it operates as a master scene supplying all believers with a common motivational ground. Monotheism and the monetary motive are structurally parallel; both let agents traverse local scenes without losing identity (hypostasis preserved).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Universal religion / Stoic cosmopolitanism / British imperial 'dressing for dinner'; the monetary motive shadowing the monotheistic motive (book pp. 43-45).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Universal motives are 'incipiently' polytheistic — they must split into adjectival sub-motives ('saints,' 'nationalisms,' 'wage slavery' versus 'capital') to handle the diversity of local scenes; Marxism applies this to the factory.

substance_types.label: Intrinsic / extrinsic substance
substance_types.gloss: The dialectical pairing of motivations-within-the-agent against motivations-derived-from-scene. Hegel pairs Matter (extrinsic, gravity-externally-referred) with Spirit (intrinsic, Bei-sich-selbst-sein). The poles invert structurally when an intrinsic principle is operationalized through external means; the intrinsic must not be confused with the unique (the shared attributes of a class also matter to a thing's nature).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Hegel on Matter and Spirit; Korzybski's 'inside-the-skin / outside-the-skin'; gerontologist's 'intrinsic resistance to disease' (book pp. 46-49).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Whenever this distinction is present, the paradoxes of substance follow. Spinoza's causa sui marks the limit: humanism makes man causa sui; supernaturalism derives human substance from God as ancestor.

substance_types.label: Rhetorical substance
substance_types.gloss: The ambiguity of substance as a deployable resource of persuasion. 'Substantially,' 'essentially,' 'in principle,' 'in the long run' — adverbs that allow a speaker to assert a thing's identity at a level of generality that cannot be falsified by the particulars. Positivists who outlaw substance reimport it covertly under 'in-principle.'
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Slave 'substantially free'; petition ruled 'substantially fraudulent' then reversed; League of Nations accepting proposals 'in principle' (book pp. 51-53).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Locates the rhetoric of substantiation as a working tactic in legal, political, and scientific discourse — including disciplines that disavow substance.

substance_types.label: Substance as point of departure (consistent / compensatory)
substance_types.gloss: Because pentad terms function as 'principles' with overlapping margins, a thinker uses a substance-term as a point of departure in two opposite manners: (i) consistently, deriving consequences from its nature ('reasons by a therefore'); (ii) compensatorily, departing from the term toward its near-antithesis ('reasons by a however'). The god-term retains its rhetorical anchor while the structure built under its name actually moves elsewhere.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: 'Naturalism' begun as man-in-nature, becoming a name for technology-and-money; 'personalism' affirming persons where persons are not paramount; Descartes giving 'new proofs of the existence of God' that subtly redefine God (book pp. 53-55).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Identifies the diachronic mechanism by which a substance-term's content evolves without changing its name — load-bearing for any historical diagnostic of philosophical idiom-shift.
substance_types.related_pentad_term: all five (any term can be a god-term)

substance_types.label: Consubstantial substance (epithetic, identificatory)
substance_types.gloss: Substance as it operates in epithets and identification-tactics: to call a man brother is to proclaim consubstantiality with him; to call him bastard is to attack his familial 'authorship.' An epithet assigns substance doubly — characterizing the object and implying an action toward it, thus serving as motive.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: 'Friend' / 'brother' / 'bastard' as substance-assignations; the entire pragmatics of injurious and gratifying speech (book p. 57).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Forward-anchors the consubstantiation apparatus of A Rhetoric of Motives (1950); shows that substantiation is observable structural reality, not metaphysical illusion.

substance_types.label: Centrality-of-substance (the synopsis-claim)
substance_types.gloss: Burke's closing thesis: even if substance dissolves under sustained scrutiny, it re-forms as soon as scrutiny relaxes; things do have intrinsic natures, and the quandaries crowd in only when we attempt to fix them definitively. The pentad is therefore secondary not as the philosopher's stone but as 'a philosopher's stone for the synopsis of writings that have sought' it. Substance-talk is universal in human discourse; the grammar of motives describes the rules under which it gets made.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Closing of the chapter — the meta-statement that all theology, metaphysics, philosophy, criticism, poetry, drama, fiction, political exhortation involve substance-tactics (book pp. 55-58).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Recapitulates the chapter as a meta-apparatus — every substance-type is a way of stabilizing motive-ascription, and the chapter as a whole is a topography of those ways.

concepts.label: Stance-family vocabulary (the *sthā- root)
concepts.definition: Indo-Germanic root *sthā- (Sanskrit sthā, German stellen) generates the Stance family — consist, constancy, constitution, contrast, destiny, ecstasy, existence, hypostatize, obstacle, stage, state, status, statute, stead, subsist, substance, system, plus Vorstellung. All derive from a concept of place or placement; tracing their ramifications could 'build a whole philosophic universe.'

concepts.label: Sub-stance as 'standing-under'
concepts.definition: Literally, a thing's sub-stance is what stands beneath / supports it — hence etymologically extrinsic to the thing, although used to designate what the thing intrinsically is. The Greek hypostasis carries the parallel sense ('standing under'); the medical hypostasis adds the 'cloacal' connotation (sediment, lees, dregs).

concepts.label: Lockean impairment of substance
concepts.definition: In the Essay Concerning Human Understanding (Bk II, Ch XXIII, 'Of Our Complex Ideas of Substances'), Locke exposes the term's incoherence: pressed for the support of qualities one can only answer 'something — he knows not what.' Burke argues that banishing the term merely conceals its functions; dramatism dwells on its embarrassments and transformative potentialities.

concepts.label: Definition as boundary-marking
concepts.definition: From de-finire (to mark boundaries). To tell what a thing is, one places it in terms of something else — to mark its boundaries is to use terms that possess at least implicit contextual reference. This linguistic structure is the source of the paradox.

concepts.label: Omnis determinatio est negatio (Spinoza)
concepts.definition: Spinoza's formula: all determination is negation. To define a thing in terms of its context is to define it in terms of what it is not; only the total context (universal substance) can be 'in itself' (kath' auto / id quod per se concipitur).

concepts.label: Kath' auto / id quod per se concipitur
concepts.definition: The Aristotelian / Spinozist criterion: 'in itself' or 'conceived through itself.' Spinoza holds that only the universal totality meets this requirement, since any single object is determined by the surrounding others.

concepts.label: Universals ante rem / in re / post rem
concepts.definition: Mediaeval debate over universals translated by Burke as: does the tribe give birth to its members (ante rem, realism), does the tribe exist in its members (in re, Aristotelian), or is the tribe merely the sum of its members (post rem, nominalism)?

concepts.label: Entelechy
concepts.definition: Aristotelian concept Burke reads as 'the individual's potentialities for becoming a fully representative member of its class' — connecting familial substance, actus/status (act-potency), and class-substance.

concepts.label: General / generic / genetic / genitive (the cluster)
concepts.definition: Four words from the same root that mark the fade from biological-familial to logical-classificatory. 'Genitive' is unambiguously ancestral; 'genetic' refers to source; 'generic' is fading the tribal note; 'general' nearly extinguishes it.

concepts.label: Hypokeimenon, hypotithēmi, ponere
concepts.definition: Greek and Latin sub-clusters: hypokeimenon ('underlying'), hypotithēmi ('to place under, assume'), and Latin pono giving thesis, antithesis, synthesis, position, proposition, opposition, composition, positive, and posit. Substance-grammar pervades the philosophical vocabulary.

concepts.label: Transubstantiation as nutritive substance
concepts.definition: Burke extends substance-grammar to ingestion: eating is the transubstantiation of external into internal elements, and the resulting consubstantiality with environment is empirically observable (Bernard's 'blood as internal environment'; Angyal's biosphere with subject and object merged in one process).

concepts.label: Second nature of language (dialectic substance)
concepts.definition: Cultural accretions made possible by the language-motive become a 'second nature' with men — symbolic communication is not merely an external instrument but is intrinsic to men as agents. The dialectic substance covers both 'the human situation' and what men are 'in themselves.'

concepts.label: Ta pathēmata mathēmata (poiēma/pathēma/mathēma)
concepts.definition: Greek proverb 'the suffered is the learned.' Burke unpacks it into three terms: poiēma (deed, act, poem), pathēma (suffering, passive condition), mathēma (the learned, knowledge, the mathematical). The triad is the dialectic of tragedy.

concepts.label: Intelligere est pati
concepts.definition: Scholastic formula: 'to understand is to be affected by.' Pati's range: bear, support, suffer, endure, experience, undergo. Knowledge is treated in terms of action-and-passion. Berkeley's idealist esse est percipi reverses the direction (actuality in terms of knowledge).

concepts.label: Actus / status pair
concepts.definition: Burke's load-bearing dyad: act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith-as-act vs. knowledge-as-state, potentiality / actuality. Articulates the substance vocabulary with the Act-Agent ratio of the pentad.

concepts.label: Philological drift (aretē, virtus, hero)
concepts.definition: Active terms become state-terms over historical time: aretē/virtus from Ares — prowess → potentiality → state-of-mind → sheer negations ('not killing, not stealing'); 'hero' from doer-of-heroic-things → potentialities-for-heroic-action → inherited reputation.

concepts.label: Causa sui
concepts.definition: Spinoza's definition of substance as 'the cause of itself.' Anchors the chapter's contrast of humanism (man as causa sui, intrinsic dignity) and supernaturalism (substance and dignity derived from God as ancestor).

concepts.label: Consistent / compensatory points of departure
concepts.definition: A pentad term used as 'principle' admits two opposite developmental directions. Consistent: derive consequences from the term's nature ('therefore'). Compensatory: depart toward the term's near-antithesis ('however'). Lets a thinker keep a god-term while diverging from it.

concepts.label: Witheriness of withinness / atop-the-atop
concepts.definition: A symbolic-poetic marker of the paradox of purity: when the inward is intensified to its absolute, it tends to its negation. Marvell's 'annihilating all that's made / to a green thought in a green shade'; Melville's 'blackness of darkness.'

concepts.label: Consubstantial epithet
concepts.definition: Burke's closing demonstration: epithets assign substance doubly — characterizing an object and implying an action toward it. To call someone 'brother' is to proclaim consubstantiality; to call him 'bastard' is to attack his familial authorship. Forward-anchors the consubstantiation theory of A Rhetoric of Motives (1950).

positions.label: Substance is structurally paradoxical, not eliminable
positions.claim: The paradox of substance is structurally inherent in the act of definition: any term for what a thing intrinsically is must, etymologically and grammatically, refer at least implicitly to what is outside the thing. Banishing the term merely conceals its functions; the dramatistic move is to study the term's embarrassments and potentialities for transformation.

positions.label: Dialectic substance is the over-all substance category
positions.claim: All other substance-types — contextual, familial, geometric, directional, nutritive, tragic, actus-status, class, universal, intrinsic-extrinsic, rhetorical, departural — are special cases of dialectic substance, since each is generated by the systematic contemplation of antinomies. Dialectic substance is the dramatistic super-category that integrates the rest.

positions.label: Actus/status is the chapter's bridge to the pentad
positions.claim: The actus/status dyad articulates the substance grammar with the pentad most tightly. It maps onto the Act-Agent ratio (acts become agentive properties become status), onto motion/rest, drama/lyric, faith/knowledge, potentiality/actuality, and onto the diachronic transformation of class-substance and political legitimacy.

positions.label: Substantiation is observable structural reality, not illusion
positions.claim: Contra scientistic abandonments of substance, the transformations Burke studies grammatically are not illusions but citable realities — observable in the tactics by which people injure and gratify one another in epithets, in legal usage of 'substantially,' in scientific deployments of 'in principle.' The pentad is a synopsis for these tactics.

philosophers_cited.name: John Locke
philosophers_cited.role: Source of the impairment-of-substance critique; Essay Concerning Human Understanding Ch. XXIII quoted at length (book p. 22).

philosophers_cited.name: Spinoza
philosophers_cited.role: Paradigm of contextual definition (universal substance = God = nature); originator of omnis determinatio est negatio and causa sui.

philosophers_cited.name: Aristotle
philosophers_cited.role: Substance considered kath' auto; entelechy and the in-re universal; God as Pure Act or eternal repose; pati and the active/passive grammar.

philosophers_cited.name: Plato
philosophers_cited.role: Theory of forms as familial-archetypal substance; the eponym-in-heaven model; mathēmata as link to the dialectic.

philosophers_cited.name: Plotinus
philosophers_cited.role: God as to proton in familial-substance; negative theology arriving at abstract Oneness through dialectic substance.

philosophers_cited.name: Hegel
philosophers_cited.role: Pure Being = Not-Being (paradox of purity); dialectic as gradual progress through self-realizing dyings; Matter (extrinsic, gravity) versus Spirit (intrinsic, Bei-sich-selbst-sein); State as 'embodiment / materialization of Spirit.'

philosophers_cited.name: Kant
philosophers_cited.role: Background figure (the chapter title echoes Kantian antinomies); not extensively cited in this chapter.

philosophers_cited.name: Leibniz
philosophers_cited.role: Doctrine of virtual innateness of ideas glossed as 'unaware awarenesses' — instance of paradox of purity.

philosophers_cited.name: Bonaventura
philosophers_cited.role: rationes seminales as combination of logical and biological descent — familial substance applied theologically.

philosophers_cited.name: Berkeley
philosophers_cited.role: esse est percipi as inversion of intelligere est pati — actuality treated in terms of knowledge rather than knowledge in terms of action and passion.

philosophers_cited.name: Descartes (via Veitch)
philosophers_cited.role: Departure-substance: questioned old dogma by 'sapping its foundations,' supplying new proofs of God that subtly changed the term's meaning.

philosophers_cited.name: Coleridge
philosophers_cited.role: rivales as opposite banks of the same stream — dialectic substance.

philosophers_cited.name: Korzybski
philosophers_cited.role: 'Inside the skin / outside the skin' as intrinsic/extrinsic distinction; aversion to Aristotelian elementarism that Burke reads as paradoxically substance-laden.

philosophers_cited.name: I. A. Richards
philosophers_cited.role: Principles of Literary Criticism — pun reducing emotion to motion.

philosophers_cited.name: Dewey
philosophers_cited.role: Naturalism's intrinsic-motive account of human nature; humanist strategy of intrinsic dignity.

philosophers_cited.name: Freud
philosophers_cited.role: 'Cloacal' motives — used to gloss the medical sense of hypostasis (sediment, lees, dregs).

philosophers_cited.name: Andras Angyal
philosophers_cited.role: Foundations for a Science of Personality — biosphere argument that subject and object merge in a single physical situation.

philosophers_cited.name: Windelband
philosophers_cited.role: Cited on Spinoza ('the deity is all and thus — nothing').

interlocutors.name: Indo-European etymological lexicography
interlocutors.role: The Stance-family etymology is the chapter's opening rhetorical apparatus; Burke uses lexical data as primary philosophical evidence.

interlocutors.name: Scholastic ontology
interlocutors.role: Universals debate (ante rem / in re / post rem), intelligere est pati, fides/intellectus, actus/potentia.

interlocutors.name: General-semantics movement (Korzybski-Hayakawa lineage)
interlocutors.role: The principal twentieth-century anti-substance polemic — Burke reads its 'inside-the-skin / outside-the-skin' as a renewed instance of the paradox of substance.

interlocutors.name: Southern Agrarians
interlocutors.role: 'I'll Take My Stand' as paradigm of scenic / purposive contextual substance (stand in Dixie versus stand for Dixie).

interlocutors.name: Marxism
interlocutors.role: Universal-motive substance applied to the factory situation; sheer work as motion becoming actus only under socialist organization; the question whether the state can 'wither away.'

interlocutors.name: Hellenistic / monastic theology
interlocutors.role: Negative theology (Plotinus) and the Christian creation-derivation as paradigms of dialectic and familial substance.

interlocutors.name: Nazi 'blood' philosophy
interlocutors.role: Bastardized familial substance — race-supremacy as tribal definition.

interlocutors.name: Twentieth-century positivism
interlocutors.role: Outlawed substance officially but reimports it covertly via 'in principle' and 'universally valid.'

tensions.label: Intrinsic / extrinsic instability
tensions.description: The same vocabulary that designates the intrinsic etymologically refers to the extrinsic. Hegel's Matter-Spirit pairing inverts when the State becomes the 'materialization of Spirit.' The gerontologist's 'intrinsic resistance' dissolves under chemical operationalization. No definition of the intrinsic can be sustained without latent extrinsic reference.

tensions.label: Actus / status petrification
tensions.description: Active terms drift into state-terms (aretē, hero, kingship) and active classes harden into property-classes; yet the underlying action does not disappear (the king's holdings retain him as king after he no longer acts; the capitalist state's property structure carries an ongoing act of expropriation). The pair captures the diachronic conversion of motion into rest and back again.

tensions.label: Paradox of purity (pure pole flips to its negation)
tensions.description: Pure being is not-being; pure personality is impersonality; pure escape is perpetual imprisonment in escape; class-motive becomes pure when set against the individual locus. Any term intensified to its absolute reverses into its dialectical antithesis.

tensions.label: Positivist self-undermining
tensions.description: Modern science and positivism officially abandon substance and causality but reimport their functions through hidden vocabularies — 'in principle,' 'universally valid,' 'intrinsic resistance,' 'tendency.' The dramatist diagnosis is that no terminology can in fact escape dialectical operations, since terminology is by definition dialectical.

tensions.label: Modesty / centrality of the pentad apparatus
tensions.description: Burke concedes that the pentad is not the philosopher's stone but is 'a philosopher's stone for the synopsis of writings that have sought the philosopher's stone.' This double-move — modesty about metaphysical reach, immodesty about analytical synopsis — is the chapter's stance on its own apparatus.

cross_pipeline_bridges.anchor: actus-status (potentia/actus; energeia/dynamis); entelechy in familial-substance; kath' auto as 'in itself' criterion; God as Pure Act in paradox of purity. Burke names Aristotle directly on book pp. 25, 27, 35, 41.

Burke 1945 predates Heidegger reception in English (Phase 0 cite-check Heidegger=0). The paradox-of-substance and the intrinsic/extrinsic instability anticipate SZ's critique of Vorhandenheit-substance metaphysics; Burke's stance-vocabulary (consist, constancy, stage, state, status, system, Vorstellung) tracks the same German metaphysical vocabulary SZ destructs.

cross_pipeline_bridges.target: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy (BCAP)
cross_pipeline_bridges.anchor: BCAP's reading of Aristotelian energeia/dynamis and pathos converges with Burke's actus-status pair and his poiēma/pathēma/mathēma triad; both treat the active-passive grammar of pati / paschein as load-bearing for the ontology of action.
Burke's stance-vocabulary etymology and his treatment of 'in itself' / 'in re' anticipate the philological method of contemporary phantasia scholarship.

cross_pipeline_bridges.target: Burke - A Rhetoric of Motives (1950, pending future pipeline)
cross_pipeline_bridges.anchor: The consubstantial-epithet substance type (book p. 57) names the apparatus that the 1950 volume develops as consubstantiation/identification. This chapter forward-anchors the entire rhetorical apparatus of Rhetoric of Motives.

Calleja's six PIM dimensions (kinesthetic / spatial / shared / narrative / affective / ludic) can be read as a substance-vocabulary for game-user motive: each dimension is a way-of-placement for the player-as-agent in the game-as-scene. Substance-type categories (contextual, directional, dialectic) map onto PIM-dimensional involvement.
Burke's contextual substance and his nutritive substance (Angyal-biosphere argument that organism/environment merge) anticipate the Umwelt analytic — agent constituted by environmental envelope.
